title: 10x Rule
author: Grant Cardone
blurb: Grant Cardone argues that most people fail not because they lack talent, but because they badly underestimate what success will take. His fix is the 10X Rule. Set targets ten times bigger than you think you need, then take ten times the action you think is required. Along the way, he sorts behavior into four degrees of action: doing nothing, retreating, normal action, and massive action. Only massive action reliably gets results. Cardone treats success as a duty rather than a luxury, and warns that aiming for average is a quiet way to fail. He urges readers to stop competing and start dominating their field, and to read fear and criticism as signs of progress. The book's tone is relentless and motivational. Its central message is simple: think bigger, do far more, and never stop expanding.

lessons.t: Why Everyone Underestimates What Success Takes
lessons.b: Most goals fail because people miscalculate the time, effort, and energy required, so they plan for far too little.
Aim ten times higher than feels reasonable, because big targets demand new thinking and even missing them leaves you far ahead.
You can take no action, retreat, take normal action, or take massive action, and only massive action consistently creates success.
Doing what most people do yields average results, and average leaves you exposed when life gets hard.
issues: scene 5: The 'rope with no slack' is broken. Two separate arcs droop from each post and end in mid-air with a gap between them. It reads as a snapped or drooping rope, which is the opposite of a taut rope with no slack, so the picture contradicts the narration. (fix: Draw one continuous straight rope stretched tight between the two posts, optionally with small strain marks at the posts. Keep the 'NO SLACK' label above it.)

scene 2: The 'COMFORTABLE' caption under the house sits almost directly on top of the headline 'But the comfort is an illusion.', with almost no gap. The chimney also cuts through the dashed roof line. (fix: Move the house and its caption up about 30px, or push the headline block down, so there is clear space between the caption and the headline. Place the chimney so it rests on the roof line instead of crossing it.)

lessons.b: Instead of chasing competitors, do so much more that you own your market and others end up chasing you.
When you see success as an obligation and read fear and criticism as signs of progress, massive action becomes a way of life.
issues: scene 1: The 'GOAL' label inside the faded amber circle on the slope is very small, roughly 14px at 1600 width, and low contrast, so it is barely readable. (fix: Enlarge the circle and set the 'GOAL' label to at least 18–20px in a darker ink or amber. Alternatively, move the label beside the circle.)

scene 3: The wallet icon sits right against the bottom of the curve, so the curve's lowest point touches or collides with the wallet's top edge. (fix: Move the wallet icon down about 20–30px, or offset it to one side, so there is clear space between it and the curve.)
